title: ERC-8004 failure: self-feedback and the fresh-address loophole
summary: The owner tries to rate its own agent and is refused. It then rates from a fresh address it controls, which the registry cannot tell apart from a real client. Only a reader that filters by trusted reviewers ignores it.

actors.label: Fresh address controlled by the owner

steps.label: giveFeedback(4242, 100, 0, "starred", ...)
steps.detail: The registry asks the Identity Registry whether the caller is the owner or an approved operator.

payload.content:
// Illustrative example, spec version Draft 2026-01-25.
ReputationRegistry(0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63).giveFeedback(4242, 100, 0, "starred", "", "", "", bytes32(0))

failures.condition: The caller owns or operates agent 4242

steps.label: giveFeedback from a fresh address
steps.detail: The same person funds a new address and calls again. Since feedbackAuth was removed, nothing ties feedback to a real interaction, so the call succeeds.

steps.label: Return NewFeedback
steps.detail: The entry is public and looks like any other.

steps.label: getSummary(4242, trustedClients, "starred", "")
steps.detail: The reader passes only clients it trusts, so the fresh address does not count. This is the only defense the text provides.
